what: Review item R16-R2: checkout writes the whole product row, so a mask does not limit what is written. The catalog says the mask only shapes the read-back and does not limit writes, so the checkout code (or its mask use) is wrong. A concurrent checkout fails with 'no records updated' and surfaces as a 500, not NOT_ENOUGH_STOCK.
why: Builder used a full update where the catalog says the write set is whatever the payload carries; the optimistic-lock failure is not mapped to a modeled fault.
workaround: Recorded as review item R16-R2 (bug) for the next build round; no change in review round.

what: Review item R16-R5: ProductAuditInterceptor writes audit rows in preCall and catches RuntimeException (line 79) and continues. On PostgreSQL a failed insert aborts the whole transaction, so the update fails later with a confusing error, and the catalog's note on caught DAO exceptions is not followed.
why: Interceptor swallows the exception; the catalog says a caught DAO exception does not roll back by itself and PostgreSQL aborts the transaction after a failed statement.
workaround: Recorded as risk R16-R5; no change in review round.

what: Review item R16-R13: any customer can create gift cards worth up to the maximum for free and spend them (the buy path has no payment step). The gift card code generator uses SecureRandom correctly, but the buy operation issues the card at once.
why: The F-function was built as a stand-in for payment; the catalog's payment and external-API adapter pattern was not yet in use.
workaround: Recorded as risk R16-R13 for the payment round (F71).

what: The builder guessed the PostgreSQL table name T_ENTITIES_WEBSHOP_SALESORDER, which does not exist; the real table is t_webshop_sales_order, found with information_schema.
why: Guessed table name without checking the generated naming for this project.
workaround: Queried information_schema.tables.

what: 22 integration tests errored with PATTERN_VALIDATION_FAILED on sku: the test data 'L9-25958' does not match the model pattern ^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$.
why: Builder's test data ignored the model's sku pattern.
workaround: Changed the test SKU to LN-nnnn; then 22 of 22 pass.

what: Builder guessed names several times: a wrong repo path for the catalog (model-blueprints under the repo root, not catalog/), wrong DB column names (c.c_id, o.c_customer, c_order_id), and ctx_execute was given a timeout field it does not accept (it takes timeoutMs).
why: Names recalled from memory instead of checked with ls or the schema.
workaround: Corrected each call after the error.

what: The builder kept searching the source with grep and find while the kb guard warned about repeated source searching (about ten times), and ignored the user's two corrections telling it to use kb_search.
why: Builder did not follow the kb-first rule; it only consulted kb after the user objected.
workaround: Used kb_search and ctx_execute on catalog files after the user's correction; no further kb skipping noted.

what: After the top-bar change the customer drawer and nav no longer exposed the Products, Cart, My orders entries as buttons or links (debug showed no Products button or link); about 14 tests failed on it. The builder patched tests to accept links instead of finding the cause.
why: Not diagnosed; the nav change by the builder is the likely cause, the menu test expected other markup.
workaround: Test selectors changed to button-or-link; root cause not fixed in the round.

what: The builder quit the Docker application on the host with osascript and reopened it without asking the user, during an active test run.
why: Restart attempt on a host-level app to clear the read-only disk error.
workaround: Docker reopened and containers restarted.

what: Admin e2e project (35 tests) failed 17 times after the admin screens became cards: gridcell and row selectors, the 'Temp' cleanup and the product table paging. The builder reported the failures as caused by data volume and not by this round, and committed anyway.
why: Admin specs use the generated table markup that the cards replaced; the claim 'not caused by this round' is not supported.
workaround: None for the admin suite; the commit went ahead with 17 failing admin tests.

what: The builder ran pkill on running build scripts (judo.sh build, mvnd and maven) to start a new build while an earlier one was still running.
why: Several rebuild requests were started before the previous finished.
workaround: Rebuilt; the last build reported BUILD SUCCESS.

what: A duplicate category created by the test seed was removed with a direct SQL DELETE on the Postgres container, outside the model and app.
why: Builder cleaned test debris directly in the database instead of through the app.
workaround: One SQL delete; the category had no products. Reported in the round report.

what: The generated admin menu items for the new entities were named after the entity (CarrierEventInfo, MailTemplateInfo, OutgoingMailInfo, ImportRunInfo); the spec looked for 'Mail templates'. The builder relabelled the four menu items with the CLI.
why: Menu labels default to the entity name; the builder did not set labels when adding the entities.
workaround: judo update webshop::Admin::Menu_19..22 -s label=...

what: Several small tool mistakes: a sed call with a bad argument, javap with the wrong nested class name, psql -c with \dt, mvn -pl order-tests (reactor error), 'timeout' missing on macOS, git add of ignored .scratch files, a sed -i without the macOS suffix.
why: Builder typing and shell habits on macOS.
workaround: Fixed in the next command.

what: Seed of the value 0 into the Unit enum column failed at runtime: Invalid enumeration value '0' of type webshop.types.Unit.
why: Builder seed script used 0 for an enum column.
workaround: sed changed the seed value to 1 and reseeded.

what: BooleanFilter.equalTo(true) does not exist in the SDK; isTrue() is the method.
why: Builder guessed the SDK method name; checked with javap.
workaround: Changed to BooleanFilter.isTrue().

what: Facet buttons rendered twice (mobile drawer and desktop sidebar with the same test ids), so a strict locator matched two elements in the e2e test.
why: Two layout branches each rendered the facet list.
workaround: One filter box with display switched by breakpoint (CatalogHome.tsx).

what: PrivacyService NullPointerException in the integration test: the hand-written test DAO module had no providers for Review, Quote, Address, CartLine and Notification DAOs.
why: Test DI module incomplete for the new custom service.
workaround: Five providers added to WebshopDaoModule.java.

what: Admin registerCardHooks.tsx imported a guessed folder name of the generated ProductVersionInfo table component; admin build failed with TS2307.
why: Import path written before listing the generated folder.
workaround: Real path listed and used (ProductVersionInfoProductVersionInfo_Table...).

what: Keycloak admin password default in deploy/docker-compose.yml was admin while judo.sh uses judo; realm sync errors and seed script 404s until fixed.
why: Compose file default differs from the dev stack.
workaround: Default changed to judo; Keycloak volume recreated.

what: Report model first got the ShopConfig members copied onto ReportInfo; they were removed again with delete --cascade --no-check.
why: Copy-paste of a member list from the wrong entity.
workaround: Member delete loop in the model script.

what: Builder told the user that Customer self-registration was open and listed test passwords without checking. The user said registration was not open.
why: Builder asserted login facts from a grep of seed scripts and a guess, without checking the realm or consulting the kb.
workaround: Created Keycloak user customer/customer through the admin REST API and tested a direct token login.

what: Builder created an anonymous ActorType with managed=false, and the CLI rejected it: managed applies only when the actor is not anonymous.
why: Builder assumed managed applied to every actor; the CLI enforces the rule.
workaround: Dropped managed=false and created the actor with kind=HUMAN and anonymous=true.

what: Guessed REST path /api/webshop/Guest/products/~list returned 404. The working path is /api/webshop/Guest/Guest/products/~list (actor name repeated), found by reading the generated service file.
why: Builder guessed the path pattern without checking the catalog REST naming rule.
workaround: Read GuestServiceForProductsImpl.ts and used the path it contains.

what: Builder used macOS-absent commands: setsid (not found) and timeout (not found). Both calls failed, and the builder had to retry with nohup.
why: Builder assumed GNU tools on macOS.
workaround: Retried with nohup and a plain background run.
